Because the internal state of a stochastic network relaxes on finite timescales, its output generally lags behind a changing environment, producing computational errors. We show that for reversible continuous-time Markov networks the error admits a universal thermodynamic bound. Decomposing the total error into representation and lag contributions, we derive an inequality relating the lag error to the entropy production rate and a memory time equal to the integrated equilibrium autocorrelation of the output observable.
